s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with variable growth pattern in a patient with history of plasma cell myeloma
salient_findings: Lesion in the right hepatic lobe with increased SUVmax on PET/CT
Lesion in segment VI with restricted diffusion on MRI
Variable lesion size over time, initially decreasing then enlarging
key_facts: Patient has IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma
Patient has undergone multiple chemotherapy regimens
Patient has undergone two autologous stem-cell transplants
Patient has undergone thalidomide maintenance and focal bone radiotherapy
Patient is asymptomatic with stable vital signs
No hepatosplenomegaly on examination
Liver function tests are within normal limits
PET/CT showed a 35 mm lesion in the right hepatic lobe with SUVmax of 6.1
MRI showed a 17 mm lesion in segment VI with moderately increased T2 signal and decreased T1 signal
Lesion has weak heterogeneous contrast enhancement and restricted diffusion on MRI
Lesion size decreased to 10 mm then enlarged to 57 × 46 mm over time

shortlist.label: Plasma cell myeloma hepatic involvement
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma and imaging shows a lesion with variable growth pattern

shortlist.label: Extramedullary plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of plasma cell myeloma and lesion characteristics are consistent with plasmacytoma

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion has imaging characteristics concerning for malignancy and patient has history of multiple chemotherapy regimens

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of multiple chemotherapy regimens and lesion has variable growth pattern

shortlist.label: Hepatic lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion has imaging characteristics consistent with lymphoma and patient has history of immunosuppression

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma and the presence of a liver lesion with characteristics suggestive of malignancy on imaging, along with the fluctuating size of the lesion, are most consistent with hepatic involvement of the patient's known plasma cell myeloma.

rejected.label: Extramedullary plasmacytoma
rejected.why: While possible, the direct involvement of the liver by the patient's known myeloma is more likely given the context and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's liver function tests are within normal limits, and there's no mention of cirrhosis or other risk factors that typically precede hepatocellular carcinoma.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease
rejected.why: There's no mention of another primary malignancy that could metastasize to the liver, making this option less likely given the patient's known history of plasma cell myeloma.

rejected.label: Hepatic lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma could present with liver lesions, the patient's history and the specific characteristics of the lesion are more suggestive of plasma cell myeloma involvement rather than a new diagnosis of lymphoma.
